about.title: THE TEAM
about.subtitle: Units behind the Hunter system.
about.story: Who's Human was born at 42 as the final ft_transcendence project. Five units joined forces to build a real-time multiplayer game inspired by Just Act Natural: cyborgs hiding among humans while a Hunter tries to expose them. What started as an academic challenge —microservices, WebSockets and in-browser 3D— turned into a cyberpunk world of its own.

manual.intro: Three rounds, rotating roles and one essential rule: looking human matters as much as scoring points.

objective.title: OBJECTIVE
objective.description: Finish the three rounds with the highest score. Every action counts and roles change between deployments.

cyborg.title: CYBORG
cyborg.description: Blend in with NPCs, avoid suspicious movement and collect items without revealing your identity.

hunter.title: HUNTER
hunter.description: Watch the city and shoot hidden players. Correct hits score points; shooting an NPC removes them.

rounds.title: ROUND END
rounds.description: A round ends when time runs out or the Hunter finds every cyborg. Roles rotate before the next deployment.

faq.title: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
faq.subtitle: Quick answers before deploying a new operation.

game.question: WHAT IS WHO'S HUMAN?
game.answer: It is a social stealth multiplayer game inspired by Just Act Natural. Players hide among NPCs while another player tries to identify them.

roles.question: HOW DO THE ROLES WORK?
roles.answer: The Hunter observes and shoots from an aerial view. Cyborgs move through the city, imitate NPCs and collect items.

rounds.question: HOW LONG IS A MATCH?
rounds.answer: Each match has three rounds. A round ends when time runs out or the Hunter finds every hidden player.

friends.question: HOW DOES THE CONTACT NETWORK WORK?
friends.answer: You can search for units, send requests and manage contacts from the network icon. Received and accepted requests create notifications.

privacy.title: PRIVACY POLICY
privacy.subtitle: What data Who's Human stores, what it is used for, and what control you have over it.

collect.title: WHAT DATA WE COLLECT
collect.body: When you create an account we store your email address and your username. You may optionally add a bio, an avatar and your preferred language. During gameplay we record match statistics (rounds played and score) and your contact list.

purpose.title: WHAT WE USE IT FOR
purpose.body: Solely to authenticate your account, show your profile to other players and run matches. We do not use your data for advertising, we do not sell it and we do not share it with third parties.

storage.title: WHERE IT IS STORED
storage.body: In the project's own PostgreSQL database, hosted alongside the rest of the services. Your password is never stored in plain text: we only store its hash encrypted with bcrypt.

cookies.title: SESSION AND BROWSER
cookies.body: We do not use tracking cookies or third-party analytics. When you log in we store an access token in your browser's local storage to keep the session open; it is removed when you log out.

rights.title: YOUR RIGHTS
rights.body: You can view and modify your data from your profile at any time, and delete your account whenever you want. When you delete it, your personal data is permanently anonymized.

academic.title: ACADEMIC PROJECT
academic.body: Who's Human is an educational project developed at 42 School, with no profit motive or commercial exploitation of the data. The service may be shut down once its evaluation is complete.

terms.title: TERMS OF SERVICE
terms.subtitle: The conditions under which you may use Who's Human.

acceptance.title: ACCEPTANCE
acceptance.body: By creating an account and using the service you accept these conditions. If you do not agree with them, do not use the platform.

nature.title: NATURE OF THE SERVICE
nature.body: Who's Human is an educational project of 42 School. The service is provided as is, with no guarantee of availability, data retention or absence of errors.

accounts.title: YOUR ACCOUNT
accounts.body: You are responsible for keeping your password safe and for the activity carried out from your account. One account per person is allowed and impersonating other users is not permitted.

conduct.title: RULES OF CONDUCT
conduct.body: It is not permitted to harass, insult or discriminate against other players, to cheat or modify the client to gain an advantage, or to attempt to disrupt or overload the service.

enforcement.title: NON-COMPLIANCE
enforcement.body: We may suspend or delete accounts that breach these rules, without prior notice and without right to compensation.

availability.title: AVAILABILITY AND CHANGES
availability.body: As this is a training environment, the service may be interrupted, restarted or changed at any time. Matches in progress may be lost during a restart.
